title: The bass choir and why the drummer needs the bass
summary: Jones says he wanted a record with five bass players and that the foundation of the music is the tympani and the bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: ...You remember, Milt, you and I made a record and I always had in my heart that I was going to make a record with 5 bass players. I always said I was going to have Richard Davis; I always said I was going to have George Duvivier; I always said I was going to have Ray Brown... And I went on down the line. But when we sat in the back room, I said, "Now I got all you people here and I'll go out here with my drum and I'll kill all you people... At last after 4 or 5 years I got all you people together. You must remember that out of the things that we did, Milt, that you were the coordinator to get what you have now going with the bass thing."
Oh, we have a wonderful bass choir. We have a very beautiful bass choir and I'm very proud of it.
Milt, it's impossible, not improbable - it's impossible, it's improbable for, as I reiterated before,
long before this, there's no way in the world that a man playing in the percussion section if he sit down with a drum, he don't know how to play with the bass fiddle. It's lost.
Well, we have to all play together...

That's what I mean. Now once he plays with the bass fiddle it's like the heart, the lungs of the body, and then he goes and he plays. But the most gratifying thing, as we were speaking about the Yale thing, it was the greatest thing that personally I have ever had a chance to see, that I'm sitting up on the bandstand. I didn't get a chance to play with you. I was playing with Duke Ellington, Harry Edison, and I played with Ray Brown. Ray Brown says, 'What am I playing?' And I said, 'Don't ask me; ask Duke Ellington.' I'm mad because I don't get a chance to play with you or George Duvivier. You and George Duvivier made me quit recording because I didn't have you to play on the bass. It's like they used to do with the Brooklyn Dodgers. 'Who's on first? Gil Hodges.' I said, 'Do you mean to tell me - who have you got playing bass with me?' I would not show up. Everybody thought that I had a whole lot of money; but they didn't understand that it's impossible for me to play, because, Milt, you must remember this - the foundation of this whole thing that we have - let's go back to the classics - you start with the tympani and the bass.
They start from the bottom. Peoples like you or Charlie Mingus or Ray Brown or what have you, you are the basics of the academy of the music field.
